## FABTECH Takeaway: Why Paint Kitchen Electrification Is Gaining Traction


As manufacturers look for new ways to improve efficiency, reduce operating costs and modernize production processes, paint-kitchen electrification is gaining more traction.


At FABTECH, North America’s largest metal forming, fabricating, welding and finishing event, Graco experts shared insights into how electric technologies are helping manufacturers rethink traditional paint-kitchen operations. Educational sessions presented by Michelle Striggow, category sales manager; Wendy Hartley, senior product manager; and Blake Erickson, senior product manager, discussed the growing interest in electric pumping technology and the role it can play in modern finishing operations.


#### Why electrification is gaining traction


For decades, pneumatic systems have been a common choice for paint kitchens. Today, however, manufacturers are reevaluating those systems as they look to increase energy efficiency, automation and process visibility.


During the FABTECH sessions, the Graco team highlighted several advantages electric technologies can offer compared to traditional pneumatic solutions, including:


- Improved control, monitoring and performance
-


Remote access capabilities


-


More consistent results and less rework


-


Easier integration into automated systems


-


Increased uptime


-


Reduced noise levels


-


Elimination of pump icing


-


Lower operating costs


-


Reduced material waste


By reducing the need for compressed air, electric systems can help manufacturers modernize paint-kitchen operations while supporting broader efficiency and sustainability goals.


#### Industry trends are accelerating adoption


Several trends are driving renewed interest in electrification across manufacturing.


Manufacturers are adapting to increased digitalization, expanding use of Industry 4.0 technologies and growing demand for production data and connected equipment. At the same time, many manufacturers are pursuing sustainable, carbon-reduction initiatives and exploring opportunities to improve energy efficiency throughout their operations.


The shift towards electric vehicles (EV), increased use of adhesive bonding and continued investment in smart manufacturing technologies are also pushing manufacturers to evaluate electric alternatives in finishing operations.


These trends are creating new opportunities for modernization and smart manufacturing throughout the paint kitchen.


#### Electric pump technology is evolving


While paint-kitchen electrification has become a growing topic of discussion, electric pump technology itself is not new. Electric pumps have been used in industrial applications for decades. However, what changed is the level of control and operational insight available through today’s systems.


Modern pump technology provides access to diagnostics, usage trends and predictive maintenance information that can help manufacturers make more informed operational decisions. Greater monitoring capabilities can help teams identify potential issues earlier, improve maintenance planning and support consistent production results.


Another factor driving interest is energy efficiency. Modern electric pump systems use up to 80% less energy than comparable pneumatic systems, helping manufacturers reduce operating costs while supporting sustainability initiatives.


#### Modernizing the paint kitchen


One of the key takeaways from Graco’s FABTECH sessions was that electrification is about more than replacing one pump technology with another.


When manufacturers consider electric solutions, they are often looking for ways to improve efficiency and operational visibility while preparing their facilities for future production demands. By combining energy savings with advanced capabilities, electric technologies can help support a more integrated and efficient finishing operation.
